citations.narrative:
***The facility recently acquired a serval (3/23/26) and three black handed spider monkeys (3/11/25) but the current
license does not authorize the use of those animals. Licenses must specifically authorize the use of each of the following
groups of animals: Group 5 (baboons and nonbrachiating species larger than 33 lbs.) and Group 6 (great apes over 55
lbs. and brachiating species) nonhuman primates; exotic and wild felids (including but not limited to lions, tigers, leopards,
cheetahs, jaguars, cougars, lynx, servals, bobcats, and caracals, and any hybrid cross thereof); hyenas and/or exotic and
wild canids (including but not limited to wolves, coyotes, foxes, and jackals); bears; and mega-herbivores (including but
not limited to elephants, rhinoceroses, hippopotamuses, and giraffes). The facility recently submitted an application to add
these animals, the licensee must obtain a new license before using any animal beyond those types or numbers of animals
authorized under the existing license.
Correct by September 29, 2026.

***There was a camel bite incident that occurred on March 28, 2026. The facility has a raised camel feeding station with
wooden deck rail around it where the public is provided feed in cups for the camels. The camel enclosure is lower with a
barrier fence placed to prevent the camels from getting too close to the feeding platform. The camels are able to reach up
and take feed from the customers. In addition there is an attendant on the platform during the public feeding. A member of
the public was able to hold their child over the rail in closer proximity to the camels which provided the camel the
opportunity to bite the child. Although several measures were in place to protect the public the current arrangements
failed to protect the public from injury. During public exhibition, any animal must be handled so there is minimal risk of
harm to the animal and to the public, with sufficient distance and/or barriers between the animal and the general viewing
public so as to assure the safety of animals and the public.
Correct by July 22, 2026.

***The facility is not storing bags of feed in the storage unit and in the trailer in a manner that protects them from vermin
and contamination. There is feed scattered on the feed bags and floor. Feed stored in this manner is an attractant for
vermin. Food shall be stored in a manner that protects supplies from vermin, food deterioration, and contamination.
Correct by July 27, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the Zookeeper onsite and the owners via Facetime.
You may appeal all or part of any inspection report by submitting a written statement contesting the findings—along with
any supporting documentation—to the Deputy Administrator. Appeals of routine, focused, or attempted inspections must
be received within 21 days of report issuance as shown by the signature line of this report.
Appeals may be sent by email to AnimalCare@usda.gov.
Appeals sent by mail should be addressed to:
Deputy Administrator
APHIS Animal Care (AC)
U.S. Department of Agriculture
2150 Centre Avenue, Building B
Mailstop #3W11
Fort Collins, CO 80526-8117
